Definition: from G1722 and a presumed derivative of the base of G939; equivalent to G1684; to intrude on (figuratively):--intrude into.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, embateúō is the word for intrude into. In Colossians 2:18, the text says "intruding into those things which he hath not seen."
TheologicalSignificance: This word, embateúō, does its job quietly — intrude into — and I leave it at that.
